en.one: A laboratory company that issues independent certificates for diamonds, gemstones and jewellery. Margins are very high and there is no debt; it passed the moat criterion, but more than half the business depends on lab-grown diamonds.
en.business: IGI examines diamonds, gemstones and jewellery and issues a report (certificate) stating their quality; it is paid per report. In the July-September 2026 quarter it issued 4.35 million reports at an average of 891 rupees each. Revenue in the quarter was 3.98 billion rupees and the EBITDA margin was 61.4%. 54% of revenue comes from certifying lab-grown diamonds. The company listed in December 2024.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. A certificate is worth what the laboratory's name is trusted for: management says the fee is 2-3% of the stone's retail price, a small cost for the buyer but a condition of the sale. The evidence is in the margin: the EBITDA margin was 60.9% in April-September 2026 (57.8% a year earlier). Management says its share in natural loose-stone certification is the highest in the industry and that it was the first international laboratory to certify lab-grown diamonds; the documents opened in this reading contain no independent market-share figure. The weak side: growth comes from lab-grown diamonds (loose stones +37% in the quarter, natural loose stones +8%); if the wholesale price of that product falls or buyers skip certification, volumes drop. Of the 4% rise in revenue per report, 2 points came from the acquired AGL and 2 points from product mix, not from price increases. Real return on equity in the last measured fiscal year (2024) was 41.1%.
en.mgmt: The promoter (a Blackstone entity) holds 76.55% of the shares; foreign institutions 8.79%, domestic institutions 5.47%, the public 9.17% (September 2026, secondary source). Part of the IPO proceeds went to buying the IGI Belgium and IGI Netherlands groups from the promoter (company filing, January 2026): this is a related-party purchase and was weighed in the D score. The company moved its financial year from December to March; the transition period is 15 months (January 2025 - March 2026). An interim dividend of 2.55 rupees per share was declared in August 2026. Management's order of priority: growth first, then acquisitions, then dividends. The gemstone laboratory AGL was acquired in January 2026; the price is not in the documents opened. Share-based pay: diluted earnings per share are about 3% below the basic figure (15.92 against 16.46 rupees for the 15-month period); the expense amount could not be read in the filing. Goodwill, pension deficit and derivative positions: looked for, not in the documents opened. Cash and bank balances are 10.75 billion rupees; debt is very small (150 crore rupees per a secondary source, possibly mostly lease liabilities; not verified).
en.latest: 21 October 2026: The company reported the July-September 2026 quarter. Revenue was 3.98 billion rupees (+31%), EBITDA 2.45 billion rupees (+39%) and net profit 1.86 billion rupees (+43%). For the six months April-September 2026 revenue was 7.69 billion rupees (+27%) and net profit 3.52 billion rupees (+37%). Management said the full-year outlook given in May (15% revenue growth, 20% EBITDA growth) will be exceeded; it gave no new figure.
risks: 54% of revenue comes from certifying lab-grown diamonds; if the price of and demand for that product fall, report volumes and profit fall.
Demand for certificates depends on jewellery sales; jewellery is discretionary spending and declines when the economy slows.
The EBITDA margin of the Indian parent company fell from 72.9% to 69.2% in the half-year; management attributes this to staff, marketing and commission costs.
The promoter holds more than three quarters of the shares; part of the IPO proceeds went to buying companies it owned. The share count rose 12.4% in five years.
The interim figures of eleven subsidiaries were not reviewed by auditors; they were consolidated on management's certification (secondary source).

en.one: A company that makes and sells watches in India under Timex and licensed brands. Sales are growing fast, but the brands belong to the parent and equity is very thin; it did not pass the moat criterion.
en.business: Timex Group India makes watches at its Baddi plant in Himachal Pradesh and sells them in India; Timex, Helix and TMX belong to its own group, while Guess, Gc, Versace, Aston Martin and others are licensed brands. In the year to March 2026 revenue was 79,859 lakh rupees (8.0 billion rupees) and net profit 7,544 lakh rupees (754 million rupees). 98% of sales are in India. The largest channel is dealers and distributors; e-commerce is the fastest growing. The company also provides IT support to group companies.
en.moat_text: The moat is weak; the company did not pass the third wall. The brands it sells are not its own: it pays the parent group a royalty for the Timex name (2,685 lakh rupees in fiscal 2026; 3.4% of revenue) and buys the licensed watches from group companies (purchases of 13,819 lakh rupees). The advantage stays with the brand owners; the Indian company is a distributor and manufacturer. The record of profitability is short: the company made a loss in five of the seven fiscal years from 2015 to 2021 (secondary source). Real return on equity ranged from 16% to 110% over five years; it is 61.2% for the last twelve months. The figure looks high because equity is thin: total equity at 31 March 2026 was 11,128 lakh rupees, of which 3,589 lakh rupees is the equity component of the parent's preference shares. The course of gross margin in the inflation years could not be examined (no margin table was read in the document).
en.mgmt: The stake of the parent, Timex Group Luxury Watches B.V., fell from 74.93% to 51.00% in a year (31 March 2026, annual report). No dividend is paid on ordinary shares; money reaches the parent through preference shares: 2,533 lakh rupees of preference dividends were paid in fiscal 2026 and preference shares of 2,290 lakh rupees were redeemed in March 2026. Preference shares of 6,482 lakh rupees remain; accumulated unpaid dividends are 1,400 lakh rupees. The parent group is also paid a royalty (2,685) and service charges (1,385 lakh rupees). Share-based pay: looked for, not in the sections read. Goodwill is negligible (non-current assets of 1,168 lakh rupees). The gratuity obligation is 1,470 lakh rupees. Contingent liabilities are 280 lakh rupees. Derivative positions: looked for, not in the sections read. The audit opinion is unmodified; a missing audit-trail feature in one accounting software was noted.
en.latest: 3 November 2026: The company reported the July-September 2026 quarter (figures read from a secondary source). Revenue was 358.01 crore rupees (243.67 a year earlier; +47%), net profit 47.11 crore rupees (30.23; +56%) and earnings per share 4.62 rupees (2.87). Half-year net profit was 72.13 crore rupees (44.90). Inventories rose from 196.93 crore rupees to 368.02 crore rupees in six months; operating cash flow fell to 38.96 crore rupees (63.96 a year earlier).

Inventories nearly doubled in six months (368 crore rupees); if sales fall short, discounts and write-downs follow.

VIESL.business: Vision Infra, yol ve inşaat şirketlerine asfalt serici, kazıyıcı, kırıcı ve benzeri makineleri kiralar; ikinci el makineleri yenileyip satar. Mart 2026'da biten yılda hasılat 60.700 lakh rupi (6,1 milyar rupi): 293,9 crore rupisi kiralamadan, 313,1 crore rupisi yenileme ve ticaretten. Ticaret satışının %80'inden fazlası yurt dışına. Net kâr 6.601 lakh rupi. Filo 30 Eylül 2026'da 571 makine. Şirket 2024-25'te NSE'nin KOBİ pazarında halka açıldı; sonuçlarını altı ayda bir açıklar.
VIESL.moat_text: Hendek zayıf; şirket 3. suru geçemedi. Makine kiralama sermayeyle kurulur: makineyi alan herkes aynı işi yapabilir, iş sözleşmeyle ve fiyatla alınır. İkinci el makine ticareti alım satım işidir. Üstünlüğü gösteren kalıcı bir rakam yok: FAVÖK marjı 2026 mali yılında %27,6 (bir yıl önce %28,7), Nisan-Eylül 2026'da hesapla yaklaşık %25,6. Reel özsermaye kârlılığı beş yılda %15,6 ile %37,4 arasında; son 12 ayda %27,1. Ama son okumalar amortisman yöntemindeki değişiklikle yükseldi (aşağıda) ve iş borçla büyüyor: 31 Mart 2026'da finansal borç 37.740 lakh rupi, özsermaye (varant avansı hariç) 22.915 lakh rupi. Serbest nakit akışı eksi: 2026 mali yılında faaliyet nakdi 17.744, makine yatırımı 26.606 lakh rupi.
VIESL.mgmt: Kurucu Gandhi ailesi payların %69,70'ini tutuyor (Eylül 2026, ikincil kaynak). Şirket 1 Ekim 2025'te amortisman yöntemini azalan bakiyeden doğrusal yönteme çevirdi. Yıllık rapora göre bu, 2026 mali yılında amortismanı 2.766 lakh rupi azalttı ve net kârı yaklaşık 2.078 lakh rupi artırdı; yani 6.601 lakh rupilik kârın yaklaşık üçte biri bu değişiklikten geldi. Yöntem ileriye dönük uygulandı; önceki dönemler yeniden düzenlenmedi. Temettü: yönetim kurulu raporu temettü önermiyor, genel kurul çağrısı pay başına 0,50 rupiden söz ediyor; belgede çelişki var. Denetçi görüşü olumlu; bankaya bildirilen stok ile defter arasında Mart 2026 çeyreğinde 4.764 lakh rupi fark not edildi. Hisse bazlı ücret, şerefiye, emeklilik açığı: bakıldı, okunan bölümlerde yok. Koşullu yükümlülük çok küçük (0,94 lakh rupi).

en.one: A small company that rents out road-building machines and refurbishes and sells used ones. Much of the jump in profit comes from a change in depreciation method; it did not pass the moat criterion.
en.business: Vision Infra rents pavers, milling machines, crushers and similar equipment to road and construction companies, and refurbishes and sells used machines. In the year to March 2026 revenue was 60,700 lakh rupees (6.1 billion rupees): 293.9 crore rupees from rental and 313.1 crore rupees from refurbishment and trading. More than 80% of trading sales go abroad. Net profit was 6,601 lakh rupees. The fleet was 571 machines at 30 September 2026. The company listed on the NSE's SME platform in 2024-25 and reports results every six months.
en.moat_text: The moat is weak; the company did not pass the third wall. Equipment rental is built with capital: anyone who buys the machines can do the same work, and jobs are won by contract and on price. Trading used machines is a buy-and-sell business. No lasting figure shows an advantage: the EBITDA margin was 27.6% in fiscal 2026 (28.7% a year earlier) and, by calculation, about 25.6% in April-September 2026. Real return on equity ranged from 15.6% to 37.4% over five years; it is 27.1% for the last twelve months. But the latest readings were lifted by the change in depreciation method (below), and the business grows on debt: at 31 March 2026 financial debt was 37,740 lakh rupees against equity (excluding warrant money) of 22,915 lakh rupees. Free cash flow is negative: in fiscal 2026 operating cash was 17,744 and spending on machines 26,606 lakh rupees.
en.mgmt: The founding Gandhi family holds 69.70% of the shares (September 2026, secondary source). On 1 October 2025 the company changed its depreciation method from written-down value to straight line. According to the annual report this cut depreciation by 2,766 lakh rupees in fiscal 2026 and raised net profit by about 2,078 lakh rupees; about a third of the 6,601 lakh rupee profit came from this change. The method was applied prospectively; earlier periods were not restated. Related-party sales are large: sales to Equipment HUB FZC were 7,280 lakh rupees in fiscal 2026 (12% of revenue), with a year-end receivable of 3,003 lakh rupees. In fiscal 2026 the company issued 5,363,336 warrants on a preferential basis at 250 rupees each (25% of the price received; convertible into shares until 15 July 2027): the share count could rise by about a fifth from 24,642,400. Dividend: the directors' report recommends none, while the AGM notice mentions 0.50 rupees per share; the document contradicts itself. The audit opinion is unmodified; a difference of 4,764 lakh rupees between stock reported to banks and the books was noted for the March 2026 quarter. Share-based pay, goodwill, pension deficit: looked for, not in the sections read. Contingent liabilities are tiny (0.94 lakh rupees).
en.latest: 5 November 2026: The board approved the April-September 2026 results (figures from secondary sources relaying the company's release). Total income was 398.92 crore rupees (287.83 a year earlier; +38.6%), EBITDA 101.99 crore rupees (+30.4%) and net profit 43.45 crore rupees (21.61; +101%). The year-earlier period used the old depreciation method; the two periods are not comparable on the same basis. Management targets revenue growth of 30% or more in fiscal 2027 and mentions outside cost pressure on margins.
risks: Much of the rise in profit comes from the change in depreciation method; EBITDA grew 30% while net profit doubled.
The business grows on debt and free cash flow is negative; if road-building investment slows, machines sit idle and the debt remains.
12% of revenue comes from sales to a related company; most trading sales go abroad.
If the issued warrants are converted, the share count rises by about a fifth.
The company is small and listed on the SME platform; it reports every six months, so information is sparse.

verify.en: The universe P/E (12.19) is the price divided by earnings per share for the year to March 2026: 326.5 / 26.79 = 12.19 (26.79 rupees: annual report). Being on the SME platform, the company reports every six months; the source has not yet processed the April-September 2026 half-year. The ratio page (9.21) uses the twelve months to September 2026: 6,601 - 2,161 + 4,345 = 8,785 lakh rupees of net profit (half-year figures from a secondary source), which matches 8,046 / 9.21 = 874 million rupees. So the ratio page is current, and the universe P/E is one half-year behind and understates profit. Two notes: (1) trailing profit is lifted by the change in depreciation method on 1 October 2025 (effect on fiscal 2026 net profit about 2,078 lakh rupees; annual report); (2) the universe market value implies 26.25 million shares (8,570.6 / 326.5), while the annual report shows 24,642,400 shares at 31 March 2026; the gap may be partial conversion of warrants, which could not be verified from a document. No fix is proposed: the September 2026 results filing could not be opened.

WAAREERTL.one: Güneş santrali kuran anahtar teslim yüklenici; Waaree Energies'in bağlı ortaklığı. İş ihale ve teklifle alınıyor, marj geriliyor; hendek ölçütünü geçemedi.
WAAREERTL.business: Waaree Renewable Technologies, başkaları için güneş santrali ve batarya depolama tesisi kurar (anahtar teslim, EPC), kurduğu santrallerin bakımını yapar ve küçük bir kendi santral portföyü işletir. Mart 2026'da biten yılda hasılat 3.331,42 crore rupi (33,3 milyar rupi), net kâr 478,65 crore rupi; yıl içinde 2.727 MWp proje tamamlandı. 18 Haziran 2026'da iletim hattı direği üreten ve iletim-dağıtım yüklenicisi olan Associated Power Structures'ın (APSPL) %55'ini 1.225 crore rupiye aldı. Temmuz-Eylül 2026 çeyreğinde hasılatın 606,13 crore rupisi bu yeni koldan, 444,98 crore rupisi güneş EPC işinden geldi (ikincil kaynak).
WAAREERTL.moat_text: Hendek yok; şirket 3. suru geçemedi. Anahtar teslim santral yapımı ihale ve teklifle alınan iştir: şirketin kendi sunumu işi "kamu ve özel ihale süreçlerine katılarak" aldığını söylüyor, ilişkili taraf fiyatının dayanağı da "teklif / benzer iş emri". Her proje yeniden kazanılır; sipariş defteri yaklaşık bir yıllık iştir (şirket 12-15 ay yapım süresi veriyor). Fiyatlama gücünün kanıtı yok, tersi var: FAVÖK marjı 2024 mali yılında %23,64, 2025'te %19,46, 2026'da %19,24, Temmuz-Eylül 2026 çeyreğinde %15,12. Reel özsermaye kârlılığı çok yüksek (beş mali yılda %14,6 ile %85,8 arasında, son 12 ayda %31,6), ama bu az sermayeyle çalışan yüklenici modelinden ve güneş yatırımlarındaki patlamadan geliyor, kalıcı bir üstünlükten değil. Tek ayırt edici yan ana ortak Waaree Energies'in panel üretimi; 2026 mali yılında ondan 731,57 crore rupilik alım yapıldı (hasılatın yaklaşık %22'si). Bu bir bağımlılıktır, şirketin kendi hendeği değil. Pazar payı birincil belgede yok.
WAAREERTL.mgmt: Waaree Energies payların %74,30'unu tutuyor (2025-26 yıllık raporu). 2026 mali yılı için temettü önerilmedi; kâr şirkette kalıyor. En büyük sermaye kararı APSPL alımı: 1.225 crore rupi, 31 Mart 2026'daki 933,83 crore rupilik net değerin üstünde ve ana işin dışında bir kol (iletim hattı direği ve iletim-dağıtım yüklenimi; marjı daha düşük). Alımdan sonra finansal borç 31 Mart 2026'daki 81,67 crore rupiden 30 Eylül 2026'da 1.412,99 crore rupiye çıktı (ikincil kaynak); çeyreklik finansman gideri 3,62'den 36,83 crore rupiye yükseldi. İlişkili taraf işlemleri büyük: 2026 mali yılında Waaree Energies'ten 731,57 crore rupi alım, ona 179,40 crore rupi satış, 88 crore rupi borç alındı (28'i geri ödendi). Genel kurula sunulan yeni sınır 746,80 crore rupi; içinde ana ortaktan %10 faizli, teminatsız, istenince geri ödenecek 250 crore rupiye kadar borç ve teminat var. Hisse bazlı ücret: çalışan pay opsiyon planı var (2026 mali yılında 66.809 opsiyon verildi, 99.223 pay çıkarıldı); gider tutarı okunamadı. Şerefiye, koşullu yükümlülükler ve teminat mektupları: bakıldı, okunan bölümlerde rakam yok.
WAAREERTL.latest: 19 Ekim 2026: Temmuz-Eylül 2026 çeyreği sonuçları açıklandı. Hasılat 1.057,84 crore rupi (bir yıl önce 774,78; +%36,53), ama artış yeni alınan APSPL'den geliyor: güneş EPC hasılatı 769,19'dan 444,98 crore rupiye indi (ikincil kaynak). FAVÖK 159,98 crore rupi (+%1,29), marj %15,12 (bir yıl önce %20,39). Net kâr 81,48 crore rupi (116,36; -%29,98); ana ortaklık payı 73,89 crore rupi, hisse başına kâr 7,07 rupi (11,16). Sipariş defteri 5.500 crore rupinin üstünde (güneş ve batarya 3.300, iletim-dağıtım 2.200). Şirket, iletim payı büyüdükçe marj yüzdesinin gerileyebileceğini söylüyor; kâr beklentisi vermedi.

en.one: Turnkey solar plant contractor, subsidiary of Waaree Energies. Work is won by tender and bid, margins are falling; it failed the moat test.
en.business: Waaree Renewable Technologies builds solar plants and battery storage facilities for others (turnkey, EPC), maintains the plants it builds and runs a small portfolio of its own plants. In the year to March 2026 revenue was 3,331.42 crore rupees (33.3 billion rupees) and net profit 478.65 crore rupees; 2,727 MWp of projects were completed in the year. On 18 June 2026 it bought 55% of Associated Power Structures (APSPL), a maker of transmission towers and a transmission and distribution contractor, for 1,225 crore rupees. In the July-September 2026 quarter 606.13 crore rupees of revenue came from this new arm and 444.98 crore rupees from solar EPC (secondary source).
en.moat_text: No moat; the company did not pass wall 3. Turnkey plant construction is work won by tender and bid: the company's own presentation says it wins work by "participating in government and private bidding process", and the basis of related-party pricing is "quotation / comparable work order". Every project has to be won again; the order book is about one year of work (the company cites a 12-15 month execution time). There is no evidence of pricing power, rather the opposite: the EBITDA margin was 23.64% in fiscal 2024, 19.46% in 2025, 19.24% in 2026 and 15.12% in the July-September 2026 quarter. Real return on equity is very high (between 14.6% and 85.8% over five fiscal years, 31.6% in the last 12 months), but this comes from an asset-light contractor model and the boom in solar investment, not from a lasting advantage. The one distinguishing feature is the panel manufacturing of the parent, Waaree Energies; purchases from it were 731.57 crore rupees in fiscal 2026 (about 22% of revenue). That is a dependence, not a moat of the company's own. No market share figure is given in a primary document.
en.mgmt: Waaree Energies holds 74.30% of the shares (annual report 2025-26). No dividend was recommended for fiscal 2026; profit stays in the company. The largest capital decision is the APSPL purchase: 1,225 crore rupees, more than the net worth of 933.83 crore rupees at 31 March 2026, and an arm outside the core business (transmission towers and transmission and distribution contracting; lower margin). After the purchase, borrowings rose from 81.67 crore rupees at 31 March 2026 to 1,412.99 crore rupees at 30 September 2026 (secondary source); quarterly finance cost rose from 3.62 to 36.83 crore rupees. Related-party dealings are large: in fiscal 2026 purchases from Waaree Energies were 731.57 crore rupees, sales to it 179.40 crore rupees, and loans taken 88 crore rupees (28 repaid). The new limit put to the shareholders' meeting is 746.80 crore rupees; it includes up to 250 crore rupees of loans and guarantees from the parent, unsecured, at 10% interest and repayable on demand. Share-based pay: there is an employee stock option plan (66,809 options granted and 99,223 shares issued in fiscal 2026); the expense amount could not be read. Goodwill, contingent liabilities and bank guarantees: checked, no figures in the sections read.
en.latest: 19 October 2026: Results for the July-September 2026 quarter were announced. Revenue was 1,057.84 crore rupees (774.78 a year earlier; +36.53%), but the increase comes from the newly bought APSPL: solar EPC revenue fell from 769.19 to 444.98 crore rupees (secondary source). EBITDA was 159.98 crore rupees (+1.29%), margin 15.12% (20.39% a year earlier). Net profit was 81.48 crore rupees (116.36; -29.98%); the share of the owners of the parent was 73.89 crore rupees and earnings per share 7.07 rupees (11.16). April-September 2026: revenue 1,982.09 crore rupees (+43.84%), net profit 200.44 crore rupees (-1.14%), earnings per share 18.18 rupees (19.45). The order book is above 5,500 crore rupees (solar and battery 3,300, transmission and distribution 2,200). The company says percentage margins may moderate as the transmission share grows; it gave no profit guidance.
risks: Work is won by tender and bid; every project has to be won again, and the EBITDA margin fell from 23.64% to 15.12% in three years.
The very high five-year return on equity covers the years of India's solar investment boom; five years do not show a full cycle, and solar EPC revenue fell 42% in the latest quarter.
The APSPL purchase is larger than net worth and was made with debt; borrowings rose from 81.67 crore rupees to 1,412.99 crore rupees in six months (secondary source).
The company depends on its parent, Waaree Energies: panel purchases, loans and guarantees come from it, and the 74.30% shareholder sets the terms of these dealings.
The source's five-year return on equity was measured on the small capital base before the purchase; the new arm's minority interest and debt pull this ratio down.

en.one: Road and infrastructure contractor. Last 12 months' profit is a one-off gain from toll-road sales; work is won by tender. Did not pass Wall 3.
en.business: Ashoka Buildcon builds highways, railways, power transmission lines and buildings in India; it also operates some of the roads it built. Work is won in public tenders. On 30 September 2026 its order book was 159.6 billion rupees: 38.7% road construction, 23.9% power transmission and distribution, 10.4% railways. Consolidated revenue in the July-September 2026 quarter was 15.0 billion rupees.
en.moat_text: There is no moat; this is why the company did not pass Wall 3. Work is won by tender and goes to the lowest bidder; the EBITDA margin of the contracting arm is around 10% (9.9% in July-September 2026). The low P/E on the page (1.39) and the high return on equity do not come from the core business: in the October-December 2025 quarter the company sold five toll-road companies to Maple Infrastructure Trust for 18.1 billion rupees and booked a one-off gain of 23.8 billion rupees in that quarter. Net profit in that quarter was 21.1 billion rupees; the total of the last four quarters is about 22.7 billion rupees. So once the sale gain is taken out, no profit is left in the last 12 months. Real return on equity is volatile for the same reason: between 10.5% and 54.6% over five years.
en.mgmt: The founders hold 54.47% (September 2026). The company has paid no dividend since 2019. The money from the toll-road sale went to debt: consolidated debt fell from 49.1 billion rupees in September 2025 to 27.8 billion rupees in September 2026; this is positive. Six more road projects are expected to be sold. Because profit came from a one-off, non-operating source, the company also did not pass the predictability-of-earnings criterion.
en.latest: 5 November 2026: In the July-September 2026 quarter consolidated revenue was 15.0 billion rupees (−18.7% year on year). The company booked a net loss of 1.19 billion rupees (a profit of 0.91 billion rupees a year earlier). The reason: a one-off expense of 3.19 billion rupees; according to the news summary, 2.37 billion rupees of it is impairment and 0.82 billion rupees is maintenance-related losses. Profit before tax and before the one-off expense was 1.91 billion rupees (2.84 billion a year earlier). Net profit for April-September 2026 was 82 million rupees (3.18 billion a year earlier). The order book stood at 159.6 billion rupees.
risks: The P/E on the page (1.39) is misleading: the last 12 months' profit consists of a one-off gain of 23.8 billion rupees from the sale of five toll-road companies. Once this gain drops out of the period the P/E will rise sharply; total profit in the last two quarters was 82 million rupees.
The core business is shrinking: consolidated revenue fell 19.6% in April-September 2026. Management had targeted growth of about 20% for fiscal 2026-27.

The business depends on public tenders and on payments by public bodies. On the February 2026 call management said a matter involving the highways authority (NHAI) had been stayed in court and that an investigation in Bihar was not expected to have a material financial impact.

One-off expenses keep recurring: 2.19 and 3.19 billion rupees were booked in the July-September quarters of the last two years. If the sale of the remaining road assets is delayed, new impairments may follow.

HINDUNILVR.business: Hindustan Unilever deterjan, sabun, şampuan, cilt bakımı, çay, kahve ve hazır gıda satar. Yılda yaklaşık 85 milyar paket ürünü yaklaşık 9 milyon satış noktasına ulaştırır. Mart 2026'da biten mali yılda hasılat 637,6 milyar rupi, FAVÖK marjı %23,6 oldu. Yıllık satışı 10 milyar rupiyi aşan 21 markası var.
HINDUNILVR.moat_text: Hendek geniş. Üstünlük markalardan ve dağıtımdan geliyor: 21 büyük marka ve yaklaşık 9 milyon satış noktasına ulaşan bir ağ. Bir rakibin aynı ağı kurması yıllar ve büyük sermaye ister. Fiyatlama gücü marjda görünüyor: FAVÖK marjı %22-24 aralığında. Reel özsermaye kârlılığı son beş mali yılda %12,0 ile %19,6 arasında kaldı, son 12 ayda %15,2. Zayıf yanı: son iki yılda büyüme cılızdı; şirket büyümeyi satın aldığı yeni markalarda (Minimalist, OZiva) arıyor. Reel kârlılık 2. surun eşiklerine yakın.
HINDUNILVR.mgmt: Sermayenin %61,90'ı ana ortak Unilever'de (Eylül 2026). Kârın büyük bölümü temettü olarak dağıtılıyor: 2026 mali yılı için hisse başına 41 rupi, toplam 96,3 milyar rupi. Şirketin net borcu yok (net borç/FAVÖK −0,54). Dondurma işi Aralık 2025 çeyreğinde ayrı bir şirkete (Kwality Wall's) devredildi; Minimalist ve OZiva satın alındı, Pureit satıldı. Yönetim yatırım harcamasını hasılatın %2'sinden %3'üne çıkarmayı planlıyor.
HINDUNILVR.latest: 28 Ekim 2026: Temmuz-Eylül 2026 çeyreğinde hasılat 180,7 milyar rupi. Şirketin açıkladığı temel satış büyümesi %15 ile son 14 çeyreğin en yükseği; satış hacmi %7 arttı. FAVÖK 40,9 milyar rupi (+%8), FAVÖK marjı %22,6 (geçen yıla göre 1,4 puan düşük). Net kâr 28,0 milyar rupi ile geçen yılla aynı; istisnai kalemler hariç %9 arttı. Marj baskısı: son çeyrekte FAVÖK marjı 1,4 puan geriledi; girdi maliyetleri yüksek. Büyüme hacimle geliyor, kâr aynı hızla artmıyor.
Reel özsermaye kârlılığı ortalaması 2. surun eşiğinde. Enflasyon yükselirse ya da kâr gerilerse şirket kalite surunda elenebilir.
Yeni ve internetten satan markalar ile hızlı teslimat uygulamaları, dağıtım ağının sağladığı üstünlüğü zayıflatabilir.
Ana ortak Unilever çoğunluk sahibi; temettü ve satın alma kararlarını o belirler.

en.one: India's largest company in cleaning, personal care and food brands. The moat is wide; it waits at the gate because the price is very expensive.
en.business: Hindustan Unilever sells detergent, soap, shampoo, skin care, tea, coffee and packaged food. It delivers about 85 billion packs a year to about 9 million outlets. In the fiscal year that ended in March 2026 revenue was 637.6 billion rupees and the EBITDA margin 23.6%. It has 21 brands with annual sales above 10 billion rupees each.
en.moat_text: The moat is wide. The advantage comes from brands and distribution: 21 large brands and a network that reaches about 9 million outlets. Building the same network would take a competitor years and a large amount of capital. Pricing power shows in the margin: the EBITDA margin is in the 22-24% range. Real return on equity stayed between 12.0% and 19.6% in the last five fiscal years and was 15.2% in the last 12 months. The weak side: growth was feeble in the last two years; the company is looking for growth in the new brands it bought (Minimalist, OZiva). Real profitability is close to the thresholds of Wall 2.
en.mgmt: The parent, Unilever, holds 61.90% of the capital (September 2026). Most of the profit is paid out as dividends: 41 rupees per share for fiscal 2026, 96.3 billion rupees in total. The company has no net debt (net debt/EBITDA −0.54). The ice cream business was transferred to a separate company (Kwality Wall's) in the December 2025 quarter; Minimalist and OZiva were bought and Pureit was sold. Management plans to raise capital spending from 2% of revenue to 3%.
en.latest: 28 October 2026: In the July-September 2026 quarter revenue was 180.7 billion rupees. Underlying sales growth reported by the company was 15%, the highest in the last 14 quarters; sales volume rose 7%. EBITDA was 40.9 billion rupees (+8%) and the EBITDA margin 22.6% (1.4 points lower than a year earlier). Net profit was 28.0 billion rupees, the same as last year; excluding exceptional items it rose 9%. An interim dividend of 19 rupees per share was declared.
risks: Price: the P/E of 30.8 on the page is calculated with a profit that includes a one-off gain of about 46 billion rupees from the separation of the ice cream business. Without this gain the multiple is higher still (42.0 on Screener.in). There is no margin of safety.
Margin pressure: the EBITDA margin fell 1.4 points in the last quarter; input costs are high. Growth is coming from volume, and profit is not rising at the same pace.
The average real return on equity is at the threshold of Wall 2. If inflation rises or profit falls, the company can be eliminated at the quality wall.
New brands that sell online and quick-delivery apps can weaken the advantage that the distribution network provides.
The parent, Unilever, is the majority owner; it decides on dividends and acquisitions.

ORIANA.one: Güneş santrali ve batarya depolama müteahhidi. Kalite surlarını geçti; iş ihaleyle alınıyor, marj daralıyor. Hendek zayıf olduğu için 3. suru geçemedi.
ORIANA.business: Oriana Power (TrueRE markası) Hindistan'da güneş santralleri ve batarya depolama tesisleri kurar. Bir bölümünü müşteri için yapar; bir bölümünü kendi proje şirketlerinde kurup işletir, sonra yatırımcıya satar. Mart 2026'da biten mali yılda konsolide hasılat 18,1 milyar rupi (+%83,7), ana ortaklık net kârı 2,52 milyar rupi (+%59,1) oldu. Teslim edilen güneş gücü 835 MW'ın üzerinde; 700 MW'tan fazla güneş ve 1.000 MWh'ten fazla depolama yapım aşamasında. Yönetime göre bekleyen sipariş yaklaşık 70 milyar rupi.
ORIANA.moat_text: Hendek zayıf; şirket bu ölçütü geçemedi. İş ihale ve teklifle alınır. Yönetim Haziran 2026 toplantısında depolama ve müteahhitlik ihalelerinde saldırgan teklifler verildiğini, düşük fiyatlı ihalelerden çekildiğini söyledi. Üstünlük, proje geliştirme ile yapımı bir arada yürütmekten geliyor ve rakamda görünüyor: FAVÖK marjı yaklaşık %23, reel özsermaye kârlılığı son beş mali yılda %31,1 ile %58,0 arasında. Ama bu üstünlük kolay aşılır ve kısa bir geçmişe dayanıyor: hasılat Mart 2022'de biten yıldaki 1,2 milyar rupiden 18,1 milyar rupiye çıktı, net kâr marjı son yıl %16,06'dan %13,91'e indi, reel özsermaye kârlılığı %45,7'den %31,1'e geriledi. Fiyatı şirket değil ihale belirliyor.
ORIANA.mgmt: Kurucu ortakların payı %57,98 (Eylül 2026). Şirket NSE'nin KOBİ pazarında (Emerge) işlem görür; sonuçlarını yılda iki kez açıklar ve mali yılı mart sonunda biter. Temettü dağıtmıyor; kâr yeni projelere gidiyor. Borç büyüyor: toplam finansal borç 31 Mart 2026'da 5,09 milyar rupi (bir yıl önce 2,71 milyar), finansman gideri 629 milyon rupi (bir yıl önce 245 milyon). Faaliyet nakit akışı 3,37 milyar rupi, yatırım nakit çıkışı 5,06 milyar rupi. Yapı karmaşık: 74 bağlı ortaklık var; satılması planlanan 14'ü konsolide edilmiyor. Şirket ana işin yanında yeşil amonyak ve hidrojen yatırımlarına giriyor. Eylül 2026'da her pay beşe bölündü (nominal değer 10 rupiden 2 rupiye). Denetçi görüşü olumlu.
ORIANA.latest: 28 Mayıs 2026: Mart 2026'da biten mali yılda konsolide hasılat 18,1 milyar rupi (+%83,7), FAVÖK 4,25 milyar rupi (+%73,4), ana ortaklık net kârı 2,52 milyar rupi (+%59,1). İkinci yarıda (Ekim 2025-Mart 2026) net kâr 1,31 milyar rupi; artış %19,0'a yavaşladı. Tek seferlik kalem yok. Yönetim, yaklaşık 238 MW'lık işler durumdaki güneş santrallerinin Actis'e satışının bu yıla yetişmediğini ve kârın beklentinin altında kaldığını söyledi. Haberlere göre satışın ilk bölümleri Eylül 2026 sonunda tamamlandı: 110 MWp için işletme değeri 5,01 milyar rupi. Nisan-Eylül 2026 sonuçları 13 Kasım 2026 itibarıyla açıklanmamıştı.
risks: Kâr büyümesi yavaşlıyor ve marj daralıyor: son yarı yılda net kâr %19,0 arttı (yılın tamamında %59,1), net kâr marjı %16,06'dan %13,91'e indi. Yönetim ihalelerde saldırgan fiyatlama olduğunu söylüyor.
Kârın bir bölümü kendi kurduğu santrallerin satışına bağlı. Satış gecikince kâr o dönem gelmiyor; gelince de o dönemin kârını yükseltiyor. Actis satışı Nisan-Eylül 2026 dönemine düşecek.
Borç ve işletme sermayesi hızla büyüyor: finansal borç bir yılda 2,71 milyar rupiden 5,09 milyar rupiye, ticari alacak 3,94 milyar rupiden 6,71 milyar rupiye çıktı.
İş kamu ihalelerine, şebeke bağlantısına ve teşvik kurallarına bağlı. Yönetim arazi, bağlantı ve onay gecikmelerini, kur ve hammadde maliyetini risk olarak sayıyor.
KOBİ pazarında işlem görüyor: sonuçlar yılda iki kez açıklanır, tablolar eski Hint muhasebe standartlarıyla (AS) hazırlanır ve 14 bağlı ortaklık konsolide edilmez.

en.one: Solar and battery storage contractor. Passed the quality walls; work is won by tender, margins are narrowing. Weak moat, so it failed Wall 3.
en.business: Oriana Power (TrueRE brand) builds solar plants and battery storage facilities in India. It builds part of them for customers; part it builds and runs in its own project companies and later sells to investors. In the fiscal year that ended in March 2026, consolidated revenue was 18.1 billion rupees (+83.7%) and net profit attributable to owners was 2.52 billion rupees (+59.1%). Solar capacity delivered is above 835 MW; more than 700 MW of solar and more than 1,000 MWh of storage are under construction. Management puts the unexecuted order book at about 70 billion rupees.
en.moat_text: The moat is weak; the company did not pass this criterion. Work is won by tender and by bid. The advantage comes from doing project development and construction together, and it shows in the numbers: the EBITDA margin is about 23% and real return on equity was between 31.1% and 58.0% in the last five fiscal years.
